name: Axiom Systems ThermaLayer Smart Parka
description:
Axiom Systems is a Tier 4 corporate manufacturer with a strong foothold in climate-adaptive apparel. The ThermaLayer Smart Parka is their flagship cold-weather piece for the GLMZ market — a mid-thigh parka in a matte-finish weatherproof shell with a detachable hood, deep cargo pockets, and a clean silhouette that does not read as obviously technical. The interior is where the technology lives: a thin-film heating element network powered by a kinetic-charge cell that tops off during normal movement, with a BCI-optional interface that allows body-temp regulation without reaching for controls.

The heating layer responds to ambient temperature and user preference, maintaining a set comfort band passively or actively. The BCI integration is optional — the jacket also works through a small haptic control panel in the left cuff. Battery life is approximately 18 hours of active heating on a full charge. It is warm, weatherproof, and comfortable without the heating engaged at all. The smart layer is the premium; the parka is already excellent without it.
functionality: Active thermal regulation via thin-film heating elements; BCI-compatible interface for body-temp preference setting; kinetic-charge cell with ~18hr active heating life; haptic cuff controls as non-BCI fallback.
what_it_says: You invest in comfort and you are comfortable with technology doing quiet work on your behalf. You do not need to announce the features — you just know you are warm.
worn_by: Spire-adjacent individuals who prefer functional over flashy
story_hooks: A character's ThermaLayer parka begins heating at maximum in a temperate room — someone is using the BCI interface to mess with them remotely
The kinetic-charge cell in a specific production batch has a flaw that causes it to store far more energy than rated — one jacket nearly started a fire
A Tier 2 knockoff of the ThermaLayer exists on the Shelf market; it uses cheaper elements and has a failure rate that has caused minor burns, but people buy it anyway

physical_description.visual_profile: A streamlined mid-thigh parka with a clean, minimalist aesthetic that reads as premium streetwear rather than overtly technical gear. The matte finish and structured shoulders give it a polished, corpo-adjacent silhouette while remaining functional enough for working-class daily wear. The detachable hood can be stowed or worn for full environmental protection.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive—designed to layer comfortably over augmentation arrays and thermal wear without excess bulk. The torso is contoured, sleeves taper slightly, and the hem hits at mid-thigh for unrestricted movement. Articulated shoulder panels allow for arm extension without riding up.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-finish weatherproof synth-composite shell (likely PTFE-bonded recycled polymer blend). Lightweight but durable, with a subtle texture that resists fingerprints and dust accumulation. Interior lined with microfiber and the thin-film heating mesh.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost suede-like matte outer surface with minimal sheen. The weave is tight and uniform, suggesting quality manufacturing. Interior heating layer feels delicate but resilient—almost imperceptible against skin.
physical_description.color_scheme: Neutral palette: charcoal, slate gray, or deep navy as primary. Subtle accent stitching in muted silver or off-white along seams. Zipper hardware in brushed steel or gunmetal. No loud branding—Axiom Systems logo is small, embroidered in understated position (shoulder or cuff).
physical_description.closures: Full-length weatherproof two-way zipper (magnetic-assisted for smooth engagement). Magnetic snap-down hood attachment points. Small haptic control panel recessed into left cuff beneath a fabric flap. No visible BCI integration port—wireless only.
distinctive_features: Detachable hood with reinforced edging and integrated micro-vents
Deep cargo pockets with internal thermal-control bypass switches
Kinetic-charge cell indicator (small LED beneath left shoulder seam—visible only when active)
Haptic feedback control panel in left cuff (subtle raised outline under fabric)
Invisible thin-film heating element network (no visible gridwork)
Optional BCI neural interface compatibility (unmarked on exterior)
Integrated cable management loop inside for augmented sensor rigs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 crossover. The technology and build quality signal mid-tier corporate manufacturing, but the design avoids the ostentatious styling of Tier 2 luxury. Accessible to working-class professionals who can afford quality gear; aspirational for Tier 4 workers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by GLMZ climate-control engineers, logistics personnel, night-shift technicians, and corpo field operatives who need gear that performs without announcing its intelligence. The smart layer is optional—meaning the wearer can choose whether to advertise their augmentation compatibility. This makes it neutral enough for those who value discretion.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in beautifully with minimal wear; the matte finish hides scuffs and dust well. After months of use, creasing develops along movement points (elbows, shoulders) but remains dignified. Well-maintained units look nearly new; heavily used ones show subtle color variation from sweat and thermal cycling.
